pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goes
   C. went
   D. goed

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. happiness
   C. quickly
   D. run

4. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

5. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops

6. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

9. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

11. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

12. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Word Classes: Primary Auxiliaries and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.4.1 Intensive reading: Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. C — went

3. D — run

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

5. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

8. B — Where is the library?

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Word Classes: Primary Auxiliaries; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 3.4.1 Intensive reading: Poetry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
